thesis.title: The problem is rarely the model
thesis.body: Most organisations are not stuck because the technology does not exist. They are stuck because nobody had time to look at their own work and ask which part of it is even worth automating. That is where we start — not with a tool, but with what you actually do all day.

look.title: Look
look.body: We spend a day where the work happens and write down what actually eats time. Not what the org chart says.

pick.title: Pick
pick.body: From that list we take one task: the best ratio of effort to time recovered. One, not ten.

build.title: Build
build.body: We build it with you — your data, your environment, open tools where possible. You see every step.

handover.title: Hand over
handover.body: At the end, someone on your side can run it, change it and switch it off. If that is not true, we did not deliver a thing — we built a dependency.

noMagic.title: Not a silver bullet
noMagic.body: Some work cannot be automated, and some should not be. We say so when we see it.

noLockIn.title: Not a dependency
noLockIn.body: What we build is yours — code, data, access. We build nothing that only runs while we are around.

noHeadcount.title: Not a big firm
noHeadcount.body: evig is small. We take on what we can genuinely see through, and decline what does not fit.

cta.heading: Tell us what eats your time
cta.body: A conversation, not a procurement process. If we are not the right people, we say so early.

meta.description: Answers to common questions about Linux & Open Source, repair, sustainability and e-waste.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.subtitle: Our answers on Linux & Open Source, repair, sustainability and responsible use of resources – in the spirit of our mission against e-waste.

faq.notListed: Can't find your question? We're happy to help in person.

items.q: Do you only work with open-source software?
items.a: No. Open source is our preferred route – for its transparency, security and longevity. Where it makes sense, we also use or integrate proprietary software, always with a focus on usefulness and sustainability.

items.q: Why is open source important to you?
items.a: Open source strengthens self-determination and repairability. It reduces dependencies and makes it possible to use devices for longer – key levers against e-waste.

items.q: What does 'Right to Repair' mean to you?
items.a: We advocate for repairable hardware, documented processes and available spare parts. This extends the lifespan of devices and preserves resources.

items.q: Do you only work with Linux, or also Windows and macOS?
items.a: We work exclusively with Linux and open-source software. We don't install proprietary operating systems (Windows/macOS). Very rarely we make exceptions when a goal demonstrably can't be achieved with open-source tools.

items.q: Do you recommend Linux for everyone?
items.a: Linux is our standard because it's resource-friendly, secure and sustainable. If proprietary tools are absolutely required, we evaluate alternatives – and discuss rare exceptions openly.

items.q: Do you support migration to Linux or open-source alternatives?
items.a: Yes. From pilot projects to full roll-out, we guide individuals, nonprofits and businesses – including training and ongoing support.

items.q: Do you repair devices that weren't bought from you?
items.a: Yes. We repair laptops, PCs and peripherals from a wide range of manufacturers – regardless of where they were purchased.

items.q: Do you repair Apple devices?
items.a: Hardware, yes – provided spare parts are available and a repair makes sense. OS installations are Linux-only; we don't install macOS or Windows.

items.q: How long do repairs take, and what do they cost?
items.a: That depends on the fault and the parts needed. We'll provide a quote on request and keep you fully informed of your options.

items.q: Do you offer data recovery and secure data erasure?
items.a: Yes. We recover data to the best of our ability and securely erase storage media on request using recognised standards (e.g. open-source tools).

items.q: Can I just drop in without an appointment?
items.a: Absolutely. For complex cases or business appointments, a quick message in advance is helpful.

items.q: How do you concretely reduce e-waste?
items.a: Through repairs, component reuse, refurbishing and responsible recycling. We also advise on long-lasting setups and resource-efficient software.

items.q: Do you accept old devices?
items.a: Yes, provided reuse or responsible recycling is possible. We inspect devices on the spot and decide transparently whether they'll be reused or dismantled.

items.q: Do you use second-hand spare parts?
items.a: Where technically sensible, we use tested second-life parts. That saves resources and can cut costs – with no compromise on function.

items.q: Why refurbished instead of new?
items.a: Refurbished devices extend useful life, save CO₂ and raw materials. With the right upgrades, they're often more than good enough – at fair prices.

items.q: Do you stock refurbished devices?
items.a: Yes. We offer carefully checked and refurbished devices with warranty – transparently documented.

items.q: Is there a warranty on your devices?
items.a: Yes. Refurbished devices come with a warranty. We state the details transparently for each product.

items.q: How do you handle my data during repairs?
items.a: Confidentially and minimally. We only access data when needed for diagnosis, and protect storage media technically and organisationally.

items.q: Do you offer certified data erasure?
items.a: We offer secure erasure procedures with a record. Just let us know what level of security you need.

items.q: Do you offer workshops or training?
items.a: Yes. Topics include: Linux introduction, repair basics, sustainable IT, open-source tools – for beginners through to advanced users.

items.q: How can I get involved or support you?
items.a: As a volunteer, partner or donor. Sharing your knowledge is also very welcome – together we create real impact.

meta.title: CO₂ calculation & sources — methodology | {orgName}
meta.description: How {orgName} estimates CO₂ savings — formula, assumptions, sources. Transparency, not marketing numbers.
meta.ogDescription: Formula, assumptions, sources for every CO₂ number on the site.

hero.title: CO₂ calculation & sources
hero.subtitle: We show where every CO₂ number on this page comes from. Conservatively rounded, always with a linked source. A smaller honest number beats a big unsupported one.

formula.heading: The formula
formula.expression: CO₂ avoided ≈ production + distribution of a new device (ADEME) × (1 − 15% refurbishment overhead)
formula.note: Conservatively rounded down to 5 kg. The usage phase is excluded on both sides — a refurbished device uses the same electricity as a new one. The calculation assumes the purchase replaces a new device.

weights.heading: Values per category
weights.intro: Based on the open data of the French environment agency ADEME (ADEME/ARCEP study, 2025 update) — full life-cycle assessments of average new devices including the phase split, published as open data and open source. We only count the production and distribution phases.
weights.footer: {pct}% refurbishment overhead deducted (transport, cleaning, testing, spare parts): Circular Computing 2021 measured ~14% — including battery swap and intercontinental transport. Our refurbishment in Zürich is local, so the deduction is conservative.
weights.noFactor: For printers & scanners, components and peripherals we deliberately show no CO₂ figure: there is no open, defensible category value. No number beats a made-up one.

limits.heading: Limits of this estimate
items: Averages: the ADEME values describe an average device of the category, not your specific model. Manufacturer PCFs (Apple/Dell) may differ.
Replacement assumption: the calculation assumes the refurbished device replaces a new purchase. Where that does not hold, the real saving is smaller.
The usage phase is excluded — it occurs equally for new and refurbished devices (Swiss electricity mix, comparatively low-carbon).
For categories without a defensible open value (printers, components, peripherals) we claim no savings.
All figures are estimates, marked with “~” and conservatively rounded down (5 kg steps).

contribute.heading: Updates & contributing
contribute.intro: This methodology is updated continuously. Calculation source code and the data linked here:
contribute.closing: Found an error or know a better source? A short email is enough:

sources.heading: Sources & context
sources.intro: All values come from open, citable sources. For context: the ISO 14040/44-verified model by Fraunhofer Austria for refurbed finds 69–91% savings versus new devices (average 80%). Our laptop figure — 150 of a 193 kg life cycle ≈ 78% — sits at the conservative end of that band. The preliminary ZHAW LCA of our upcycling project (−82.7% GHG) independently confirms the order of magnitude.

founding.title: A spin-off born of conviction
founding.subtitle: The same roots, a bolder path
founding.p1: evig was founded in {foundingYear} in Zurich — as a spin-off from Zurich's circular-IT scene, out of Revamp-IT. Since 2003, that non-profit association has been turning old hardware back into usable computers: repairing them, reinstalling Linux and free software, passing them on instead of scrapping them — and opening access to technology for people on a small budget. Good, important work, and the ground evig grew from.
founding.p2: Out of that work we built the platform — marketplace, AI assistant, workshop — and a techno-optimist vision: making access to intelligence, to AI and robotics, affordable for everyone, fast and beyond Zurich. Revamp-IT stays with what it does well — repair and reuse, at a calm, local pace. A different goal, a different tempo.
founding.p3: So we walk our path independently. evig keeps the roots of the circular economy and aims them at the age of intelligence — full ownership, no committee to convince, a genuine market-and-quality model, open and independent. Revamp-IT's history stays Revamp-IT's; evig writes its own.

electronics.title: Electrical appliances

textiles.title: Textiles
textiles.body: Clothes, shoes and other textiles: alterations and repairs instead of buying new.

more.title: More to come

category.title: Computers are electrical appliances
category.body: Laptop, desktop, monitor or peripheral — repairs by {org} belong to the electrical-appliances category and are therefore eligible.

location.title: In the heart of Zurich
location.body: Our workshop and shop are at {address} — inside the city area where the bonus applies.

mission.title: Repair instead of discard
mission.body: That is exactly why {org} has existed for over two decades. The repair bonus makes what we already do even cheaper for you.

impact.heading: Why it matters
impact.intro: The repair bonus is part of the city's circular economy — and it replaces the former disposal coupons. The direction is clear: repair instead of throw away.

coupons.title: From discarding to repairing
coupons.body: The city used to subsidise disposal with coupons. The repair bonus flips the incentive: it rewards keeping things in use for longer.

repairs.title: ~{repairs} repairs
repairs.body: That is how many subsidised repairs the city expects over the three-year pilot.

climate.title: ~{co2} tonnes of CO₂
climate.body: That is how much greenhouse gas the additional repairs are meant to save — CO₂ equivalents that would otherwise go into new production.

who.a: Everyone resident in the City of Zurich. Each person gets up to CHF {max} per calendar year.

howMuch.q: How much do I get back?
howMuch.a: {percent}% of the repair cost, up to CHF {max} per year. On a CHF 120 repair, you get CHF 60 back.

carryOver.a: If you do not use the full bonus on one repair, the remaining balance stays available for further repairs within the same calendar year.

what.a: At the start of the pilot, electrical appliances and textiles. More categories will follow depending on demand.

devices.a: Yes. Computers, laptops and similar IT equipment are electrical appliances — exactly the repairs {org} offers.

revampit.q: Can I redeem the bonus at {org}?
revampit.a: The bonus is settled exclusively through the city platform {platform} — that is where you see which businesses take part. Repairs at {org} fall into an eligible category (electrical appliances); check on {platform} whether and how you can claim them.

cta.heading: Repairing pays off
cta.body: Find a repair business on {platform} — or bring your device straight to {org}.

meta.description: How donated computers become reliable devices again: secure data erasure, testing, Linux, warranty — and what happens when a device cannot be resold.

hero.title: A device’s journey
hero.subtitle: From donation to a new home: how an old computer becomes a reliable device at {org} — or a source of valuable parts.

journey.heading: From donation to a new home
journey.intro: Every donated device follows the same careful, transparent and traceable process.

donation.title: Donation or return
donation.body: Individuals and organisations give us retired equipment, either at our location or through collection.

intake.title: Intake and condition assessment
intake.body: Each device is registered, visually inspected and assigned a clear condition grade.

wipe.title: Secure data erasure
wipe.body: All storage media are securely erased following NIST 800-88. Previous data cannot be recovered.

refurbish.title: Testing and refurbishment
refurbish.body: Hardware is tested, cleaned and sensibly upgraded. We then install an open-source operating system such as Linux.

quality.title: Quality control and warranty
quality.body: A final inspection confirms the result. Refurbished devices receive a {months}-month warranty.

rehome.title: A new home
rehome.body: The device reaches the marketplace at a fair, solidarity-based price, ready for a second life.

paths.heading: Not every device is sold
paths.intro: Not every donation can be reused, but nothing is wasted. Every device follows one of three paths.

refurbish.title: Refurbish and sell
refurbish.body: Most working devices are refurbished and passed on through the marketplace.

parts.title: Recover parts
parts.body: Working components such as RAM, SSDs and power supplies are recovered from devices that cannot be sold.

recycle.title: Recycle responsibly
recycle.body: Anything unusable goes to SWICO-certified recycling. No component enters household waste.

cta.heading: Help close the loop
cta.body: Buy refurbished technology or give your old device a second life.
cta.openNote: The process and software are open: adopt, improve and share them for your own local circular workshop.

meta.title: The vision
meta.description: Intelligence should be reachable by anyone, anywhere. Why evig exists — and the inequality we are here to close.

hero.title: Intelligence should be reachable by anyone, anywhere.
hero.lede: Compute, artificial intelligence, and — soon — robots. Within reach of people, not just institutions and the wealthy.

thesis.title: The gap that decides all the others.
thesis.p1: We talk about inequality of income, and of wealth. But those are symptoms. The inequality that shapes a life most today is access to intelligence — and it comes in two forms.
thesis.ai: Artificial intelligence. Someone who can afford a frontier AI subscription learns faster, works better, and reaches opportunities — a better job, new skills, ideas they could not reach alone — that stay closed to someone who cannot.
thesis.robot: Embodied intelligence — robots. A robot that vacuums and mops takes real work out of a life; the dishwasher and washing machine did it before, and a humanoid will do far more of it soon. What they hand back is the scarcest thing there is: time, and the energy to use it.
thesis.pull: Intelligence is the one inequality that compounds.
thesis.p2: Those with access grow more capable and freer every year; those without fall behind — automatically, without anyone deciding it. That is why it is the gap worth closing: give a person access to intelligence, artificial or embodied, and you hand back their time and multiply what they can do with it. Not equal outcomes handed down — an equal shot at the tools that let anyone raise themselves.

origin.quote: A refurbished laptop is the cheapest on-ramp to intelligence that exists.
origin.p1: evig grew out of Zurich's circular IT — out of Revamp-IT, where since 2003 tired laptops and computers are turned back into usable machines: repaired, reinstalled with Linux, given a second life instead of a landfill. That work is good for the planet. But we saw what the recycling framing missed: the same machine that would have been e-waste is, set up right, a doorway to the most powerful tools humanity has ever built.
origin.p2: Circular economy and access to intelligence turned out to be the same act, seen from two sides. We built a platform around that idea, and we wanted to carry it fast and far. Revamp-IT stays true to repair and reuse — good work, at a local pace. We wanted to go further: so in 2026, in Zürich, we walk on independently. Same roots, bolder destination.

diff.title: Good because it is affordable. Affordable because it is good.
diff.intro: The world we came from often passes on merely good enough: take the scrap, harvest the parts, hand it along. We do it differently. evig is a market-and-quality model, run as a non-profit association in formation. The difference shows up in three promises.

p1.title: Complete machines, not parts
p1.body: No fragments, no bin of maybes, no selling someone a project. Everything in the evig marketplace is a working machine — and, in time, a working robot. If it is listed, it runs.

p2.title: Quality is a promise, not a lottery
p2.body: When we say a machine is great for live-coding music, the software is already installed, it is the right software, it is configured correctly, and it works the moment you open the lid. Fitness for a real purpose is the product — not a spec sheet.

p3.title: Hardware, software, and knowledge — together
p3.body: Owning the box is not the point; doing the thing is. Capable hardware, set up and ready, handed over with the workshops and know-how to actually use and keep it. Hardware without software is a paperweight. Software without knowledge is a locked door.

research.eyebrow: We do the research — in the open
research.title: An organisation with a point of view worth following.
research.p1: You cannot honestly make intelligence reachable if you do not understand it deeply — and the frontier moves every week. New models, new hardware, new robots, new ways to run capable AI on humble machines. Every promise we make rests on someone doing that work.
research.pull: Research is the engine under the curation.
research.p2: We publish what we learn — notes and writing on affordable AI, intelligence on second-life hardware, open robotics, repair, and sovereignty over your own tools. Openly, because knowledge in circulation is the same idea as hardware in circulation. It makes evig worth following, and it brings the right people on board. Our research is our recruiting.

afford.title: Not only bought. Raised for.
afford.intro: Access should not depend only on what is already in your wallet. Alongside buying outright, evig is building ways for people to raise their way to intelligence.

w1.title: Subscription crowdfunding & pooled financing
w1.body: Communities, classes and groups raising funds together so a person or a project can reach the tools they need.

w2.title: Shared-subscription pools
w2.body: Splitting the running cost of the AI and software subscriptions themselves — so the price of intelligence is shared, not shouldered alone.

w3.title: Give a device, fund a tool, sponsor a seat
w3.body: Donate a working machine, fund a specific piece of kit, or sponsor a workshop place. No middleman, no markup.

afford.close: This is what the tagline means. <lime>Raise for longer:</lime> raise the funds, raise the machine's life, raise the ceiling on who gets to take part — and keep it raised.

future.title: Computers — and robots.
future.p1: Today the marketplace is computers. That is the wedge, not the whole. Robots are becoming the next general-purpose tool, the way the personal computer once did — and the same logic applies: useful only if it works out of the box, honest about what it can do, and paired with the knowledge to put it to work.
future.pull: Humanoid robots are not sold second-hand yet. They are barely sold new.
future.p2: That window will not stay closed for long. When it opens, evig intends to be the first store that does it right — robots that are complete, tested, purpose-proven, and backed by the workshops to use them; new, and in time given a second life the same way we give laptops one now. Being early and being right are not the same thing. The only way to be both is to already be doing the work. That is what the research is for.

close.title: Two ways to move this forward.

support.title: Back evig
support.body: For foundations, grant-makers and patrons who believe access to intelligence should not depend on a wallet.

build.title: Join the work
build.body: For people and partners who want to research, repair, teach, and put good tools in more hands.

close.commercial: Building on our platform products? hirnli and kivvi are open, independent projects with their own home — get in touch. Kept separate from the association, by design.

footer.legal: evig — eternal — is a non-profit association (Verein) in formation in Zürich, Switzerland. hero.title: Statutes
hero.subtitle: The constitution of {orgName} — open to read before it is adopted.

draft.title: Draft — not yet adopted
draft.body: {orgName} is being founded. These statutes are a draft and have not yet been adopted by any founding assembly. They do not yet establish an association or any rights. We publish them anyway — because a constitution should be readable before it is adopted, not only afterwards.

adopted.title: Adopted
adopted.body: These statutes were adopted at the founding assembly of {adoptedOn} and have been in force since.

authoritative.title: The German version is authoritative
authoritative.body: This translation is provided for understanding. Only the German version is legally binding.

source.title: Where this document comes from
source.body: These statutes live in the public source-code repository of {orgName}. Every change is traceable there as a single dated revision — retroactively as well.

name-sitz.title: Name and registered office
name-sitz.body:
Under the name {orgName} there exists an association within the meaning of Art. 60 ff. of the Swiss Civil Code (ZGB).

The registered office of the association is in Zurich.

The duration of the association is unlimited.

zweck.title: Purpose

mittel.title: Resources

beteiligungen.title: Participations
beteiligungen.body:
In order to fulfil its purpose, the association may hold participations in legal entities or establish such entities.

Such participations are held as an investment of assets and remain subordinate to the purpose. The association does not exercise management in the companies concerned.

Income from participations accrues entirely to the purpose of the association.

erwerb.title: Acquisition of membership
erwerb.body:
Natural persons and legal entities that support the purpose of the association may become members.

The board decides on admission. A rejection does not have to be justified.

erloeschen.title: Termination of membership

beitraege-haftung.title: Fees and liability
beitraege-haftung.body:
The general assembly sets the annual membership fee.

Only the assets of the association are liable for its obligations. Any personal liability of the members and any obligation to make additional contributions are excluded (Art. 75a ZGB).

organe.title: Bodies

generalversammlung.title: General assembly

vorstand.title: Board
vorstand.body:
The board consists of at least two members. It constitutes itself.

If the employment or the compensation of a board member is resolved upon, the board must consist of at least three members.

The term of office is two years; re-election is possible.

The board holds all powers that are not expressly reserved to another body. It conducts the day-to-day business and represents the association externally.

The board has a quorum when the majority of its members are present. Minutes are kept of the deliberations and resolutions.

zeichnungsberechtigung.title: Signatory authority
zeichnungsberechtigung.body: The association is legally bound by the joint signature of two members of the board.

entschaedigung.title: Compensation and abstention
entschaedigung.body:
The members of the board hold their office on a voluntary basis as a matter of principle.

Actual expenses are reimbursed against receipts. Lump-sum expense allowances are excluded.

Appropriate compensation may be paid for work actually performed. It is determined by the general assembly.

Where a matter concerns the personal interests of a member of a body — in particular their employment or compensation — that member abstains. They take part neither in the deliberation nor in the decision. The abstention is recorded in the minutes.

Compensation paid to members of the bodies is disclosed in the annual report.

revisionsstelle.title: Auditors
revisionsstelle.body:
The general assembly may appoint auditors.

If the legal conditions for a statutory audit are met (Art. 69b ZGB), the general assembly appoints auditors in accordance with the applicable provisions.

offenlegung.title: Disclosure
offenlegung.body:
The association publishes its statutes, the composition of its board and, annually, the annual report and the annual accounts.

Publication takes a form that makes subsequent changes traceable.

As long as the association is not legally exempt from taxation, it issues no donation receipts and makes no statements claiming recognised charitable status.

geschaeftsjahr.title: Financial year
geschaeftsjahr.body: The financial year corresponds to the calendar year. The first financial year ends on 31 December of the year of foundation.

statutenaenderung.title: Amendment of the statutes
statutenaenderung.body: Amendments to these statutes require the approval of two thirds of the votes cast at the general assembly. Amendments to Art. 2 (purpose) and Art. 17 (allocation of assets) are reported to the cantonal tax authority.

aufloesung.title: Dissolution and allocation of assets
aufloesung.body:
The dissolution of the association requires the approval of two thirds of the votes cast at the general assembly.

Upon dissolution of the association, its assets pass to another tax-exempt legal entity domiciled in Switzerland that pursues the same or a similar purpose.

The repayment of contributions to members and any other distribution of the assets to the members are excluded.

inkrafttreten.title: Entry into force
inkrafttreten.body: These statutes were adopted at the founding assembly and have been in force since.

meta.title: Access to intelligence
meta.description: The division for reachable artificial intelligence: an assistant that comes with the platform, on hardware people can afford.

hero.title: Intelligence should not depend on what you earn.
hero.lede: Whoever can pay for an expensive subscription learns faster, works better and reaches opportunities that stay closed to everyone else. That gap widens on its own. Closing it is the work.

thesis.title: The gap that widens all the others
thesis.body: Intelligence is the meta-resource: it compounds. Give two people the same problem and the one with intelligence on tap pulls ahead — and keeps pulling ahead. So we do not treat access to AI as a feature bolted onto a shop; it is the same mandate as affordable hardware. A used laptop, set up properly, is the cheapest on-ramp to artificial intelligence that exists.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.body: Every page of this platform carries an assistant that knows the context of that page and answers questions about it. It belongs to the platform and is not a separate product — no second subscription, no separate login.

sharing.title: Shared access
sharing.body: A good AI subscription costs around CHF 22 a month on your own — precisely the threshold where the gap opens. Split four ways it is CHF 5.50. On this platform you can share one subscription with others and pay only your share.

hardware.title: The machine to run it
hardware.body: Software without a device is a theory. That is why hardware and assistant are not separate departments here: the machines in the marketplace are set up so that on the day they change hands they can already do the thing they were bought for.

sovereignty.title: Sovereignty
sovereignty.body: We aim for open models wherever they hold up, and traceability wherever we depend on outside providers. Where an external service answers, that should be visible rather than hidden.

noLab.title: Not a lab
noLab.body: We do not train large models of our own. We build the bridge between people and the models that already exist.

noMagic.title: Not a miracle
noMagic.body: An assistant gets things wrong. We say what it is good for — and what you should still ask a person about.

noLockIn.title: Not a one-way street
noLockIn.body: What you do here should belong to you. A division you cannot leave would be the opposite of access.

cta.heading: Start with the machine
cta.body: The cheapest way into artificial intelligence is a good used laptop that somebody set up properly.

pillars.heading: {count, plural, one {One route} other {# routes}}, one goal
pillars.subtitle: AI and robotics are shifting who can do which work. We are working to make sure access to them does not depend on what someone earns — through devices, through help, through software, through training, and through showing up where the work happens.

hardware.title: Machines good enough for real work
hardware.body: Used laptops you can genuinely work on, plus GPUs and the hardware AI runs on — chosen, tested, affordable. No printers, no e-waste with a price tag. That a machine kept in use also helps the environment is the consequence, not the sales pitch.

technicians.title: Find someone who will fix it
technicians.body: Repair and IT help should be as easy to find as a ride: post what is wrong, get offers from technicians nearby, pick one. Not wait until somebody has time.

software.title: Linux and open software
software.body: An eight-year-old laptop often runs better under Linux than it did the day it was bought. We set it up, show the open alternatives to expensive software — and tie nobody to a vendor.

training.title: Retraining for a labour market with AI
training.body: AI and robots are taking over tasks people live on. Those who can work with them lose less and gain more. Workshops that teach exactly that — on real tasks, not on slides.

adoption.title: Putting AI and robotics to work
adoption.body: For organisations that know something has to change but not where to start. We look at the work actually being done and build alongside you — until something runs.
